seo_title: Cost of Living in Tel Aviv 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Tel Aviv per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Israel's business capital, with the most developed IT industry in the Middle East and a large Russian-speaking community. For Jews — a path through repatriation; for everyone else — through a work visa and startups.
pros: The most developed IT industry in the Middle East with salaries in dollars
A large Russian-speaking community and accessibility of the language
A warm climate with a 7-month swimming season
A repatriation programme for Jews (the Law of Return)
Access to the Schengen Area for holders of an Israeli passport
cons: Some of the highest rental prices in the world
Geopolitical tension and the missile threat
Religious restrictions on the Sabbath and holidays
A hot, humid summer of +35°C and stuffiness

visa_steps.title: Repatriation (Aliyah)
visa_steps.description: For people with Jewish roots: filing documents through the Sokhnut, a review, an A-1 visa, then citizenship.

visa_steps.title: B-1 work visa
visa_steps.description: Through an employer's invitation for specialists. Processing takes 2–4 months.

visa_steps.title: Teudat Zehut
visa_steps.description: An internal identity document. Without it you can't open an account or sign a rental agreement.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Bank Hapoalim, Bank Leumi, Discount Bank — open accounts with a teudat zehut and residence permit.

visa_steps.title: Bituach Leumi
visa_steps.description: Registration with the social insurance fund. Grants access to state healthcare after 6 months.

faq.question: Who qualifies for repatriation to Tel Aviv?
faq.answer: Those with Jewish roots up to a great-grandparent. Documents are reviewed by the Sokhnut and the Ministry of Aliyah.

faq.question: Can I work without Hebrew in Tel Aviv?
faq.answer: Yes, in IT, startups and high-tech English is the main language. But for everyday life and healthcare Hebrew is essential.

faq.question: How much does rent cost in Tel Aviv?
faq.answer: From 1,500 dollars for a studio, from 2,500 for a one-bedroom in the centre. One of the most expensive rental markets in the world.

faq.question: Which banks are in Tel Aviv?
faq.answer: Bank Leumi, Hapoalim, Discount, Mizrahi-Tefahot. All accept citizens with a teudat zehut; it's harder for foreigners.

faq.question: Is it safe in Tel Aviv?
faq.answer: The city is safe in terms of everyday crime, but there are periods of escalation (rocket attacks). There are bomb shelters everywhere.

faq.question: What about children in Tel Aviv?
faq.answer: Russian schools and groups are available (Shuvu, Shevil), as well as private international ones with tuition from 12,000 dollars a year.

reviews.text: I went through Aliyah within a year: citizenship, a mortgage, a job at a startup. Salary in dollars, my daughter at the Shevil school. The downside — the cost of living is very high.
I got a work visa through a startup and pay 3,500 dollars for an apartment by the sea. The language is hard, but the IT scene in Tel Aviv is unique.
